curriculum.text: use developing knowledge of the meanings of words and morphemes (i.e., bases, prefixes, and suffixes) to read and spell words

worksheet.title: Adding -ing to Words
worksheet.subtitle: A suffix that means it is happening now

parts.text: A suffix is a word part you add to the end of a base word. Add -ing to each base word to show the action is happening now. Then read the sentences.

parts.label: Read the page 3 times. Colour a face each time you read it.

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children learn that -ing is a suffix (a word part added to the end of a base word) that shows an action is happening now. They build words by adding -ing to a base, then read the new words in decodable sentences. All base words use sounds they already know.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 20 minutes)
text: 1. Say 'A suffix is added to the end of a word. -ing means it is happening now.'
2. Model the first one: jump + ing = jumping. Read it together.
3. Children build the other words, then read each sentence on their own.
4. Children read the whole page three times and colour one face each time.

parts.title: Answer key
text: Build the word: jumping, helping, singing, reading.
Note on spelling: these base words just add -ing (no letter change). (Later lessons cover doubling, e.g. run -> running, and dropping silent e, e.g. make -> making.)
Sentences read: The frog is jumping. We are reading a book. The kids are playing ball. She is singing a song. He is helping his mom.

parts.title: Ontario curriculum link (official wording)
text: B2.3 — use developing knowledge of the meanings of words and morphemes (i.e., bases, prefixes, and suffixes) to read and spell words.
In plain terms: children use word parts — here the suffix -ing — to read and spell longer words and understand what they mean.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: reading the whole word as one chunk. Cover -ing, read the base, then add -ing.
Make it easier: do the build section together out loud before writing.
Make it harder: ask children to add -ing to run and make (these change spelling) and explain the rule.
You'll know it worked when: the child reads -ing words smoothly and explains that -ing means it is happening now.
